prompt:
Edit the supplied image, which is our generated temple establishing frame. The user has LOCKED THIS EXACT CAMERA FRAMING. Preserve the camera height, distance, lens, crop, composition, sunrise sky, horizon, low sun at left, tower silhouette and scale, palm landscape, pavilion position and size, water tank and steps, people, and seated Ganesha identity. Do not pull the camera back, raise it, zoom, tilt, rearrange buildings, change architecture or replace the idol. Maintain the same dimensional illustrated finish, warm light direction and polished floor reflections.

Change only the amount of wedding decoration. Dress this existing temple for a lavish, tasteful South Indian wedding so that it feels richly prepared for a celebration rather than sparsely decorated:

1. On the main gopuram, add several well-spaced horizontal tiers of full marigold-orange, ivory-jasmine, deep-red and green-leaf garland swags, gracefully following existing architectural ledges. Add fuller floral framing around its existing entrance. Keep stone carving visible between floral bands; do not cover the entire tower with flowers or change its outline.
2. Along BOTH side colonnades, enrich the existing floral scallops into layered orange-and-white swags, with vertical flower strings and mango-leaf torans at the outer column edges. Add tidy flower arrangements and banana-leaf accents beside a few column bases. Keep every aisle physically open.
3. Enrich the existing front pavilion roof-beam garlands and its OUTER front column decorations with fuller orange, white and restrained deep-red floral trim. Keep the center entrance, idol, inner pedestal, rear sightline and interior column faces visible and unchanged. There must never be a floral wall or opaque curtain behind Ganesha.
4. Fill the visually empty side-floor areas with intricate but restrained white kolam outlines and circular red-orange-white floral rangoli beside the shrine, fine flower-petal borders along the steps and outer aisles, and symmetrical rows of small brass diyas. Add several substantial brass standing lamps to the SIDES of the approach. Keep the central flight route over the tank and through the pavilion completely unobstructed.
5. Dress the visible water-tank rim with low floral edging, additional small diyas and a few more floating flower-and-lamp bowls, preserving plenty of open reflective water. Add scattered white, orange and red petals over the paving and a light, delicate shower of individual tiny petals in the midground. Airborne petals should be sparse enough that the skyline, tower and Ganesha remain clear.

The effect is lush, ceremonial and layered, with warm glints on brass and soft reflections from the new flowers and lamps. Keep decorations believable in size and physically attached where appropriate. No extra tower or shrine, no new foreground canopy, no banners, no text, no excessive smoke, no giant floating flowers, no bright electric string-light grid, no material changes to the architecture. Preserve the entire original frame's composition; only add the requested festive dressing.
